I1.quote: Searched the full text (abstract, Method, Results and discussion, Tables 1-3, Figs. 1-7, Conclusion) for any gravimetric, volumetric (Sieverts) or flow measurement of gas-phase H2 uptake, sample, instrument or isotherm; none found. All uptake values (5.14 and 7.51 wt%) are DFT (SIESTA) computations.

I5.quote: Based on the density functional theory calculations, we predict that the Yttrium-dispersed capped-carbon nanotubes (CCNY) can serve as a high-capacity hydrogen storage material.

notes: Purely computational DFT study. Method: "All the geometry optimization and the energy calculations have been performed by the ab initio SIESTA code" (main, p. 2 (1054), Method). Uptake is computed: "the weight percentage in this structure can reach 48.3811/(360.321 + 533.4351 + 48.3811) = 5.14 wt%" (main, p. 4 (1056), Results and discussion). Conclusion: "we hope this predication will promote experimental studies" (main, p. 6 (1058), Conclusion). Uptake values in the Introduction (8.2, 4.2, 0.8, 6.1 wt%) are quoted from other work. Not a review; record is_retracted false and no retraction notice in the PDF; no duplicate-data statement.
